name: Kondowole (Malawian Toasted Sesame Seeds)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
steps: In a dry frying pan or skillet, toast the sesame seeds over medium heat.
Stir the seeds continuously to ensure even toasting and prevent burning. The seeds are ready when they turn golden brown and release a nutty aroma.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the toasted sesame seeds cool for a few minutes.
Sprinkle salt over the seeds according to your taste preference and mix well.
Heat a small amount of vegetable oil in the same pan over low heat.
Add the toasted sesame seeds to the pan and stir to coat them evenly with the oil. This step helps to enhance the flavor and crunchiness of the seeds.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the kondowole cool completely before serving.

culture.text: Kondowole is a staple of Malawian cuisine that is eaten predominantly in the northern region of Malawi. It is made from cassava flour and water. It is a very sticky meal and resembles that of the Malawian nsima, Tanzanian ugali, or English posho. It is mostly cooked on the floor because of its texture as it is normally tough to run a cooking stick through hence a lot of strength is needed.
